text:
[Council File 26-0916; CD 9]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
ARTS, PARKS, AND CITY FACILITIES COMMITTEE REPORT relative to declaring City-owned property located adjacent to and west of the corner of 39th Street and Flower Drive, and City-owned property adjacent to 3947 South Figueroa Street near 3900 South Figueroa Street, as Exempt Surplus Land.
Recommendations for Council action, pursuant to Motion (Price – Rodriguez):
1. DECLARE the City-owned property located adjacent to and west of the corner of 39th Street and Flower Drive, consisting of 917 square feet, and the City-owned property adjacent to 3947 South Figueroa Street located near 3900 South Figueroa Street, consisting of approximately 2,218 square feet of the underlying property (collectively, City-owned Property) as “Exempt Surplus Land”, pursuant to the California Surplus Land Act. The City-owned Property was formerly excess right-of-way that is vacated pursuant to California Streets and Highways Code (Sections 8300 – 8363).
The City-owned Property constitutes surplus land as defined in Government Code Section 54221(b), in that it is land owned in fee simple by the City for which the City’s governing body has determined the land is not necessary for the City’s use. The City-owned Property qualifies as “exempt surplus land” under Government Code Section 54221(f)(1)(E), because:
a. It is a former right of way.
b. It will be conveyed to LMP USC PROPERTY OWNER LLC, which is the owner of property adjacent to the City-owned Property.
Furthermore, the City-owned Property is not located within any of the areas described in Government Code Section 54221(f)(2), which would preclude the City-owned Property from qualifying as exempt surplus land.
2. DIRECT the General Services Department, with the assistance of the City Attorney and City Administrative Officer (CAO), to take all necessary steps and prepare all required documents to effectuate the sale of the parcel(s).
3. FIND and DETERMINE that the City-owned Property, as described in the Motion, is no longer required for use by the City and that the public interest is best served by its disposal.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
Neither the CAO nor the Chief Legislative Analyst has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: A motion to declare two city-owned properties, one near 39th Street and Flower Drive and one next to 3947 South Figueroa Street, as Exempt Surplus Land.
